transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-03
Time: 09:00 AM UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Alvarez (Cobalt Head Infra), Devon Park (Cobalt SRE), Anika Bose (Cobalt ML Lead), Noah Rivera (Redwood CSM)
Shared links: pilot_metrics_2027-11-02.xlsx, runbook_ramp_2027-11-03.md
Summary: Quick review of last week's throughput runs; focused on smoothing burst-induced tail latency and reducing cold-KV spikes. Agreed to test lower concurrency cap with slightly higher batch windows and a 3-hour soak. SE will circulate new config and notes on warmup behavior.
Topics: throughput harmonization, continuous batching knobs, concurrency targets, queue shaping, KV-cache warmup, SLOs and next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Liam Chen: all right everyone good morning, thanks for hopping on. quick roll call?
[00:09] Marta Alvarez: Marta here.
[00:11] Devon Park: Devon on -- SRE.
[00:13] Anika Bose: Anika, ML.
[00:15] Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood SE.
[00:17] Noah Rivera: Noah, CSM.
[00:20] Liam Chen: cool. agenda — recap last soak, review anomalies, propose tuning, agree soak plan, action items. sound good?

[01:02] Priya Nair: quick recap from our side: last week's 2-hour soak hit the target p50 around 80ms but p95 jumped during burst windows to ~420ms, p99 spiked to 1.2s at two points. we dug in and saw two correlated things: KV-cache coldness after long idle, and the batching window shrinking because concurrency jumped higher than expected which caused smaller batches and more overhead per token.

[02:15] Devon Park: yeah we saw that in the traces — there were about three 30-40s windows with increased CPU on the node that lines up with cache misses. Also weirdly a few requests were routed to a fallback smaller model, that added extra latency.

[03:10] Anika Bose: just to add, model footprint change shouldn't be the cause — we pinned version — but our client side had a spike in parallel requests from one downstream worker. so concurrency is honest here.

[04:05] Liam Chen: great, so two knobs: raise batching hold slightly to allow more continuous-batching aggregation, and cap concurrency per-worker at a sensible target to avoid tiny batches. Priya, what's the plan?

[04:34] Priya Nair: proposed config: increase batch_window_ms from 8 to 20ms for this workload, set concurrency target to 10 per instance (we saw good throughput at 10-12 but 12 increased p99), and enable a short KV-cache prewarm on reconnects to reduce first-request penalty. also recommend enabling prefix caching for predictable routes.

[05:22] Marta Alvarez: curious on impact to tail during normal traffic, do we expect p50 to degrade?

[05:31] Priya Nair: small p50 bump maybe 5-10ms in steady state because batches will wait a bit longer, but p95/p99 should drop significantly — it's a traded-off latency vs efficiency. we estimate token cost per request lowers because of larger average batch sizes.

[06:10] Devon Park: okay that trade seems reasonable. can we see a simulated run with mixed burst shape?

[06:18] Priya Nair: yes — I ran a 30-minute synthetic with a Poisson burst pattern; attached in pilot_metrics_2027-11-02.xlsx. results: average batch size rose from 3.1 to 7.8, p99 dropped from 1.2s to 460ms, CPU utilization smoothed.

[07:05] Anika Bose: good. what about fallback behavior — you mentioned requests were routed to a fallback smaller model, why did that happen?

[07:15] Liam Chen: two reasons: one, our smart routing had an availability threshold and it fell below during a node churn so it routed to a cheaper variant; two, in some rare cases our fallback policy kicks in when queuing latency crosses the configured SLO.

[07:48] Devon Park: can we disable fallback entirely during the POC? That routing change confounds the numbers.

[07:55] Priya Nair: we can set a strict policy for the pilot: prefer same model, do not fallback unless full outage. we'll flip that for the soak.

[08:18] Marta Alvarez: about KV-cache prewarm — how invasive is that for our infra?

[08:25] Priya Nair: lightweight; it's a short background warmup on a reconnect event that issues a small sample of recent prefixes; no data is persisted externally and keys are ephemeral. it's compatible with KMS encryption — we just warm the in-memory KV.

[08:52] Anika Bose: does that require extra tokens / cost?

[08:57] Priya Nair: negligible — tiny sample traffic. cost-wise it's part of the pilot usage. we can keep it optional.

[09:20] Liam Chen: let's talk about concurrency target. earlier you said 10 per instance. what was baseline?

[09:28] Priya Nair: baseline was 18 which gave great throughput but led to tiny batches because requests arrived unsynchronized. at 18, average batch size dropped to 2-3 often.

[09:43] Devon Park: we're using AWS m6i-based dedicated nodes, is there any node-level tuning we should do?

[09:50] Priya Nair: for m6i we typically reduce hyperthreading for inference but more importantly ensure the network buffer settings allow steady egress; those are standard infra tweaks — we'll list them in the runbook.

[10:25] Noah Rivera: quick interjection — security note, Marta asked last week about audit logs and KMS. are those still fine with the proposed config?

[10:34] Liam Chen: yes, nothing changes on audit retention — all calls are logged and the private deploy option still integrates with KMS/HSM. we will re-share the SOC2 pack per your request.

[11:02] Marta Alvarez: good. can we confirm data residency constraints? we have a couple EU regions pinned, we don't want cross-region cache prewarm hitting US.

[11:12] Priya Nair: prewarm respects region; we'll scope the warmup to the same VPC/region. we'll add a note in the runbook.

[11:45] Anika Bose: timeline — if Priya shares config Friday, when can we run the soak?

[11:52] Priya Nair: I can share by end of day Friday (2027-11-05). you can schedule the soak for Monday-Tuesday window; recommended 3-hour soak to capture recurrent churn.

[12:10] Devon Park: monday morning works, I'll schedule and attach the load script.

[12:18] Liam Chen: good. next — metrics to capture. Priya listed p50/p95/p99, avg batch size, KV cache hit rate, request routing log (to ensure no fallback), and CPU/mem. anything else?

[12:33] Anika Bose: please also capture queue wait time histogram and number of inflight tokens per instance.

[12:39] Priya Nair: will do. I'll include tail-latency histogram where we bucket 50/90/95/99/999.

[13:05] Marta Alvarez: for acceptance criteria — what are we agreeing on to call this tuning successful?

[13:12] Liam Chen: propose: p95 under 500ms for the 3-hour soak, p99 under 800ms, KV-cache hit rate > 92%, sustained throughput within 5% of baseline peak, and no model fallback events.

[13:36] Devon Park: those numbers look reasonable. can we also mark a rollback plan if we see failed conditions?

[13:44] Priya Nair: yes — rollback is the previous batching window and concurrency cap, which we can flip via the console and takes effect within ~30s. we'll document the exact steps.

[14:05] Liam Chen: great. quick note about cost: if you want a Dedicated burst cushion we can allocate short-lived extra capacity for peak windows; that's a pricing add-on.

[14:16] Marta Alvarez: we may need that for holiday spikes but for now we'll do the soak without burst; please send pricing.

[14:29] Liam Chen: will do.

[15:02] Priya Nair: small gotcha we noticed — when you run the soak with many short-lived clients, the socket churn causes a slight warmup hiccup; we recommend either connection pooling at client or a jittered start-up to avoid synchronized reconnects.

[15:22] Devon Park: noted. our load script currently tears down clients every 30s — I'll change that to reuse connections.

[15:45] Anika Bose: one more question on telemetry — can we get token-level costs per model variant?

[15:52] Liam Chen: yes, the console has token-level breakdown and per-route cost. we'll give you a sample report.

[16:10] Marta Alvarez: perfect. any other blockers?

[16:15] Devon Park: none on infra.

[16:18] Anika Bose: none on ML.

[16:20] Liam Chen: okay wrapping up: Priya will share configs and runbook Friday; Devon schedules a 3-hour soak for Monday; Liam sends Dedicated burst pricing and SOC2 pack. we'll reconvene after soak for results review — propose Thursday same time.

[16:45] Noah Rivera: I'll book Thursday 09:00 UTC tentative and include the artifacts.

[17:05] Marta Alvarez: thanks everyone.

[17:12] Liam Chen: thanks, meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription: some names auto-corrected, occasional filler and overlapping talk.
